summary: Forest Service lookout on Eagle Rock above State Highway 299 near Del Loma, in use by 1933, abandoned by 1975; rock and mortar remnants remain.

facts.status_note: The lookout is gone. The register notes rock and mortar base remnants and a survey marker on the site.

events.note: New fire guard posted at the lookout by August 1933, with a telephone line to the Big Bar ranger station
No register build year. An August 1934 item describes a crew completing the building, so the building was likely finished that year
A 1975 Caltrans survey description calls it the site of an abandoned lookout; no closing date given

corrections.current: Eagle Rock Lookout Site (Arapaho-Roosevelt National Forest)
corrections.proposed: Eagle Rock Lookout Site (Trinity National Forest)
corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts page places Eagle Rock in Trinity National Forest, in Trinity County. The register's Arapaho-Roosevelt forest label does not match the site.
The register notes rock and mortar base remnants on the site. 'ruins' (remains only) fits better than 'gone'.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1933 items call it the new lookout, with a fire guard posted there; the August 1934 item describes crews still completing the building. The register gives no build year, so 1934 is the year the building appears to have been finished, not necessarily the first year of use.

notes_for_editor: Name in the record carries the wrong forest (Arapaho-Roosevelt, from the register); the Forest Lookouts page says Trinity National Forest. See corrections. Build year is unclear: the lookout was in use by August 1933, and the building was being completed in August 1934. The 'lookout house' design comes only from the 1975 survey description. Staffing is limited to the 1933 fire guard; the 1940 mule story is about supply, not staffing. No source on current access or ownership beyond the forest, and no source describing the site now beyond the register's remnants note. Record coordinates (40.743083, -123.326017) were not checked against the sources. The register's foundation photo (Mark Nelson) is already in the record, so no new photos were added.
